title: Visual shader Texture2DParameter default Type "Data" results in washed out colors in Mobile/Forward+
body:
### Tested versions

4.6.1.stable

### System information

Godot v4.6.1.stable - macOS Sequoia (15.7.4) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Metal (Mobile) - integrated Apple M2 Pro (Apple8) - Apple M2 Pro (10 threads) - 16.00 GiB memory

### Issue description

In the visual shader editor when adding a Texture2DParameter node this has the default Type set to "Data". 
Using this as is in a sampler to set a shader albedo color works as expected in Compatibility renderer (see below).

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c03c96bb-90b1-41a7-90f9-da163a8b26d8)

However, if we change to Mobile/Forward+ renderer, this results in very washed out colors:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e1a04304-6d3c-4b9c-b8d8-5aa2e532e408)

I couldn't find any documentation anywhere what this "Type" is supposed to be for, but the issue appears to be the "Data" type setting. Changing this to "Color" instead makes the texture colors correct again on Mobile/Forward+ as well (also works on Compatibility).

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/260c4f80-09a2-45d2-b0ce-da61cb66a180)

I'm not sure what the Data type is supposed to do, or if this is the expected behavior of it, but at the very least it introduces some hard to figure out lighting/color issues that could easily be avoided by just making Color the default type instead for new Texture2DParameter nodes. And if the issue is caused by this Data type not being supported in either Compatibility or Mobile/Forward+ perhaps a warning should be issued to help users understand why the shader now produces a very different result after switching renderer. 

### Steps to reproduce

- Create a new Compatibility mode project
- Make a simple 3d scene with a camera, a light and a mesh instance to apply our material to.
- Create a new ShaderMaterial and a Visual Shader for this shader material
- In the visual shader add a Texture2D sampler connected to the fragment albedo color
- In the visual shader add a Texture2DParameter and connect this to the Texture2D sampler (observe that it is default Type:Data)
- On the ShaderMaterial resource assign the default icon as the Texture2DParameter texture
- Observe the camper preview to see the mesh with the assigned material shows the icon texture as expected.
- Switch the project over to Mobile renderer
- Observer the material now renders a lot lighter.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[shader_texture.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25527642/shader_texture.zip)
